content.text:
Read CHALLENGE.md, docs/requirements.md, materials/office-policy.md and snapshot.schema.json.
Write planning/spec.md: a table with columns ID, Requirement, Source, Check. One row per
requirement, IDs R-01 onward. Requirement is one sentence that a test or an inspection can
check. Source names the file and section and quotes the exact words. Check says how we will
know it is met: the test, the file to inspect, or the command. Do not add anything the files
do not say. Do not write any code.
I’ll read the four source files and the repository instructions, then write `planning/spec.md` with exact quotes and a check for each requirement.

The sources cover extraction, routing, recovery, shared operation, verification, and submission. I’ll give each independently checkable obligation a row and keep workload context separate from requirements; the files don’t specify performance thresholds.

Created [planning/spec.md](planning/spec.md) with 80 requirements, numbered R-01 through R-80, exact source quotes, and verification checks.

No code was written. Whitespace checks passed.

Use the plan-from-spec skill on planning/spec.md. Write planning/plan.md only; write no code
and no tests yet.
I’ll use the plan-from-spec skill to turn `planning/spec.md` into ordered build steps and a test plan, writing only `planning/plan.md`.

I’ve read all 20 messages. They provide cases for missing dates, conflicts, embedded instructions, corrections, withdrawals, and identifier mismatches. I’m planning a Python CLI with mocked provider calls and persistent shared state, with each test assigned to one build step and all 80 requirements mapped to a test or inspection.

The draft has 12 build steps and 40 test cases, with quoted evidence for the expected facts from all 20 messages and the authored paraphrase. I’m checking test ownership and coverage now. Capture verification, pushing, and Classroom submission are listed as future external checks, not completed work.

Created [planning/plan.md](planning/plan.md) using the plan-from-spec skill: 12 ordered steps, 40 planned test cases, and coverage for all 80 requirements.

Only that file was written. No code or tests were added.

I’ll follow the plan in order, committing each step’s failing tests as `Test first: <step>`, then its passing implementation as `Step <n>: <step>`. I’ll run the whole suite after each step and stop if it fails. Tests will use saved mock responses, avoid API_KEY and real model calls, and assert the plan’s source-derived facts.
T-01 fails as expected: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'access_requests'`. I’ll commit the failing test and fixtures before creating the mock provider.

Step 1 is committed: `21cc6d9` contains the failing test and `726c289` the implementation. The whole suite passes (4 tests). Next are T-02–T-04 for schema validation, source identity, decoded quotes, and 200-word messages.

T-02–T-04 fail as expected because `access_requests.validation` is missing. I’ll commit them before implementation. Since no JSON Schema library is installed, I’ll validate the supplied schema’s limited vocabulary with the standard library and document that scope.

Step 2 is committed and all 7 tests pass. T-05–T-20 now fail as expected because the intake and routing modules are missing. Their assertions use the plan’s expected facts, transcribed separately from the mock replies and before any application run.

Step 3 passes all 23 tests. I corrected one test setup error: the withdrawal variant removed its ID from the message but still quoted the original message. Its evidence now matches the edited source; the expected routing is unchanged. Next are the malformed-output, provider-error, refusal, and interrupted-response cases.
T-21–T-24 fail as expected: the failure-handling `process` function does not exist yet. I’ll commit these tests, then implement explicit error records and completion-status checks.

Step 4 is committed and all 27 tests pass. For step 5, I’ll test the provider adapter through an intercepted HTTP transport, using saved success, refusal, and incomplete-response fixtures. Tests will inject a dummy credential directly and will not read API_KEY.

T-25 fails as expected because `access_requests.openai_provider` is missing. The saved fixtures follow the [Responses API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create) and [structured-output format](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs?api-mode=responses). I’ll commit the test before implementing the adapter.

Step 5 is committed and all 28 tests pass. Next I’ll add persistence tests for unchanged reruns, changed source, failed retries after success, batch omissions, and settings/policy refresh. Those tests will be committed before the store implementation.
T-26–T-31 fail as expected because `access_requests.store` is missing. I’ll commit them before adding durable attempts, source hashes, current records, and separate history.

Step 6 passes all 34 tests. The store reuses unchanged successful work, keeps changed-source results in history, and makes a failed retry visible as the current result. Next I’ll test overlapping operators, stale workers, and interrupted output publication.

T-32 fails as expected because `access_requests.publication` is missing. I’ll commit it before adding transactional claims, stale-worker protection, and publication of matching queue/extraction generations.

Step 7 is committed and all 35 tests pass. Its test confirms that two operators leave one current result per document, a stale worker cannot replace a newer revision, and a crash before publication leaves the previous generation readable. Next are scheduling and recovery.

T-33–T-36 fail as expected because the scheduler is missing. I’ll commit them before adding bounded workers, renewable leases, delayed transient retries, and recovery after a terminated process. The workload tests use saved mock replies and make no throughput guarantee.

The step-8 tests pass, including killed-worker recovery and mock workload runs of 400 and 2,000 messages. Processing took about 4 and 28 seconds respectively in this run; those are observations, not throughput guarantees. The whole-suite check is running now, and I’ll stop if it fails.
Step 8 passes the whole suite (39 tests). I’ll commit it, then add T-37 for the CLI: intake, queue inspection, resume, retry, history, and consistent exports.
T-37 fails as expected: the package has no CLI entry point. I’ll commit the test, then add the operator commands and retry guidance that includes the selected database path.

Step 9 passes the whole suite (40 tests). I’ll commit it, then add the accuracy-comparison test. That test will keep the denominator fixed at 252 scalar fields across 21 documents, including missing records and extraction errors.

T-38 fails as expected because the accuracy module is missing. I’ll commit it before implementation. Its negative controls require one wrong permission, one omitted record, and one failed extraction to produce 25 scalar mismatches without shrinking the denominator.

The mock accuracy run reports 252/252 scalar matches, 63/63 route matches, 21/21 quote-support checks, and 24/24 issue-category checks. These verify the fixture-backed pipeline, not live model accuracy. The whole suite is running before I commit step 10.

I noticed a concurrent README edit. I’ll preserve it when adding the required setup and operating documentation in step 11. The accuracy test and mock deliverables are ready; step 10 is still waiting on the whole-suite check.
Step 10 passes the whole suite (41 tests). I’ll commit its comparison command and mock deliverables, then add the step-11 documentation smoke test.

T-39 fails as expected because the README lacks the documented commands. I’ll commit the smoke test, then add setup, recovery, configuration, and operating-limit documentation while preserving your README text.

T-39 passes in a clean temporary workspace. It runs mock intake and queue commands, reproduces the 252-field comparison, and checks the handover artifacts. I also removed environment access from the starter test so it no longer touches API_KEY. The whole-suite check is still running.

Step 11 passes the whole suite (42 tests), with the run saved in `planning/test-run.txt`. I’ll commit the documentation and evidence, then add T-40 for offline submission readiness. Entire reports capture enabled, and the commits contain automatic checkpoint links.

T-40 fails as expected because the submission-readiness module is missing. I’ll commit it before implementation. It will check the required artifacts and repository-link shape; capture/commit verification, pushing, and Classroom submission will remain explicit external checks.
